title: Simultaneous Quantification of Selected Kynurenines Analyzed by Liquid Chromatography-Mass Spectrometry in Medium Collected from Cancer Cell Cultures
protocol: Weigh the reagents in a vial with highest accuracy (0.3 mg each).
Dissolve the reagents in 300 μL of solvent to obtain a stock solution of 1 g/L.
Dissolve 3NT in 1% (v/v) formic acid (FA) in water.
Dissolve Kyn, 3HAA, and XA in dimethyl sulfoxide (DMSO).
Dissolve 3HKyn in water acidified to pH 2.5 with hydrochloric acid (HCl).
Place the vial in an ultrasonic bath for 1 min.
Store stock solutions at -20 °C.
Weigh 280 mg of activated charcoal and add 5 mL of liquid medium.
Shake the tube with medium and charcoal on a see saw rocker for 2 h, set speed to 50 oscillations/min.
Centrifuge the tubes at 6000 x g for 15 min.
Carefully collect the supernatant without disturbing the sediment.
Repeat centrifugation if necessary to remove all charcoal residues.
Filter the supernatant using a 0.45 µm syringe filter.
Ensure that the charcoal pretreated culture medium is deprived of kynurenines traces by running a pilot sample on LC-MS as described in step 6.3.2.
Repeat steps 2.1-2.4 if necessary.
Spike the charcoal pretreated culture medium with 0.75 µL of 0.1 g/L 3NT solution.
Add four standards (3HKyn, 3HAA, Kyn, XA) at least at six different concentrations to cover calibration ranges.
Maintain the final volume of each sample at 150 µL.
Vortex well after adding standards.
Use 1.5 mL centrifuge tubes for sample preparation.
Add 150 µL of cold methanol containing 1% (v/v) formic acid into each tube.
Tightly close the tubes and vortex well again.
Incubate the samples at -20 °C for 40 min.
Centrifuge the samples at 14,000 x g for 15 min at 4 °C.
Collect supernatants into new tubes after centrifugation.
Do not disturb the sediment during collection.
Transfer 270 µL of the supernatant into the glass vial using an automatic pipette.
Put the vials into the evaporator and gently evaporate until dry.
Use the appropriate program for water/methanol fractions to evaporate volatile components.
Do not apply temperature higher than 40 °C and avoid over-drying.
Check the evaporation status after 30 min.
If necessary, continue evaporation (e.g., add extra 10 min).
Avoid over-drying.
Remove the vials from the evaporator.
Reconstitute each sample in 60 µL of 0.1% (v/v) formic acid in water.
Add the solvent into the vial containing the residual material.
Tightly close the vials and vortex-well.
Transfer the sample into a 1.5 mL tube and spin at 14,000 x g for 15 min at 4 °C to separate the precipitated protein.
Without disturbing the protein pellet, transfer the supernatants into chromatographic vials with conical glass inserts using an automatic pipette.
Tightly close the vials.
Check for the presence of air bubbles in the insert vial and remove them if necessary (e.g., by vortexing).
Transfer the chromatographic vials containing samples into LC autosampler.
Spike the charcoal-pretreated culture medium with 0.75 μL of 0.1 g/L 3NT solution and standards of four kynurenines at one concentration from the linear range of calibration curves.
Maintain the final volume of the sample at 150 µL.
Prepare mobile phase solvents for LC-MS system: Solvent A, 20 mmol/L ammonium formate in ultrapure water (pH 4.3 adjusted with formic acid).
Prepare mobile phase solvents for LC-MS system: Solvent B, 100% acetonitrile.
Dissolve 15.77 g of crystalline reagent in 50 mL of ultrapure water to make a 5 mol/L stock solution of ammonium formate.
Stir until all residuals dissolve.
Filter the stock solution through a 0.45 µm membrane to remove any residual debris.
Store the filtered stock solution at 4 °C.
Prepare Solvent A by adding 4 mL of 5 mol/L ammonium formate to 980 mL of ultrapure water in an amber glass bottle and stir well.
Immerse a stirring bar into the solution.
Put the bottle with the solvent on a magnetic stirrer.
Immerse a pH electrode into the solution.
Control the pH under stirring by adding formic acid stock solution dropwise using an automatic pipette with 0.2 mL tip to obtain pH 4.3.
Adjust the volume up to 1 L with ultrapure water and stir well.
Filter all solutions through a 0.22 µm membrane.
Start LC-MS control and data acquisition software.
Purge the LC system with the mobile phase to remove bubbles and prime all solvent channels.
Ensemble a guard column to protect the analytical column from clogging.
Flush the guard and analytical column (C18, 2.1 x 100 mm, 1.8 µm) with 100% acetonitrile for about 30 min.
Then flush the columns with 100% solvent A until a stable pressure in the column is observed.
Set the appropriate LC parameters in the data acquisition software.
Set up the gradient program: 0-8 min solvent B 0%; 8-17 min solvent B 0-2%; 17-20 min solvent B 2%; 20-32 min solvent B 10-30%; 32-45 min solvent B 0%.
Set the mobile phase flow rate at 0.15 mL/min.
Set the total analysis run time for 45 min.
Set the column temperature at +40 °C.
Set the injection volume at 10 µL.
Apply ionization parameters: single ion monitoring (SIM), positive ionization, nebulizer pressure of 50 psi, +350 °C drying gas temperature, drying gas flow of 12 L/min, and 5500 V capillary voltage.
Select the analyte monitoring ions for 3HKyn m/z 225.0 (scan period: 2-6 min, fragmentor voltage: 100 V).
Select the analyte monitoring ions for Kyn m/z 209.0 (scan period: 6-12 min, fragmentor voltage: 80 V).
Select the analyte monitoring ions for 3HAA m/z 154.0 (scan period: 12-18 min, fragmentor voltage: 80 V).
Select the analyte monitoring ions for 3NT m/z 227.0 (scan period: 18-23 min, fragmentor voltage: 100 V).
Select the analyte monitoring ions for XA m/z 206.0 (scan period: 23-45 min, fragmentor voltage: 100 V).
Construct a worklist.
Run samples on the LC system.
Before analyzing experimental samples, run at least three blank samples (Solvent A) and one QC sample.
Open the data analysis software.
Load results obtained for the QC sample.
Check the position of analyte peaks on the chromatogram.
Adjust time gates when signals shift beyond expected positions to collect appropriate analyte signals.
Add calibration standards into the worklist in the data acquisition software.
Run the calibration standards in triplicates.
Integrate and measure the peak area corresponding to 3HKyn at a retention time of about 4.4 min.
Measure the peak area corresponding to Kyn at a retention time of about 10 min.
Measure the peak area corresponding to 3HAA at a retention time of about 16 min.
Measure the peak area corresponding to 3NT at a retention time of about 21 min.
Measure the peak area corresponding to XA at a retention time of about 30 min.
Construct individual calibration curves for each metabolite using a spreadsheet program.
Plot the value for a ratio of analyte peak area over the 3NT peak area versus the concentration of the analyte.
Analyze the blank sample (charcoal-pretreated culture medium spiked only with 3NT) to ensure there is no trace of the studied analytes in the medium.
Subtract the obtained value from each calibration point if necessary.
Check the linearity of each calibration curve.

Create a slope-intercept linear equation for each analyte, where y corresponds to the ratio of the analyte peak area versus 3NT peak area, a is the slope, x is the analyte concentration (µmol/L), and b refers to the curve intercept.
Plot the graph ‘y’ versus ‘x’ to generate the calibration curve.
Add a linear trendline to the chart.
Display the calibration curve equation and regression coefficient on the chart.
Ensure that the regression coefficient is > 0.990.
Prepare and/or analyze mismatched calibration standards once again if necessary.
Optionally, change the concentration range of the calibration curve.
Analyze QC samples to check system performance before analyzing experimental samples.
In case of incompatibilities (± 20% deviation from reference value), prepare new calibration curves.
Plate studied cancer cells (MDA-MB-231 or SK-OV-3) in DMEM containing 4.5 g/L d-glucose, 10% fetal bovine serum (FBS), 2 mmol/L l-glutamine and 1 U penicillin/streptomycin.
Culture cells at 37 °C in a humidified atmosphere of 5% CO2 to expand them for the experiment.
Passage cells at 80% confluency.
Detach cells from culture dish using trypsin.
Seed cells on 12-well plates at a density of 0.3 × 106 cells per well and place in an incubator overnight.
Aspirate culture medium the next day.
Add fresh DMEM with or without addition of studied compounds, depending on experimental design.
After 48 h, collect medium above cells (about 500 µL) into a 1.5 mL tube.
Centrifuge at 14,000 x g for 5 min to remove cell debris.
Collect supernatant and store at -80 °C until analysis.
Save cellular pellet from step for protein estimation.
Freeze samples at -20 °C.
Prepare samples for LC-MS analysis.
Thaw the frozen sample at room temperature and mix well.
Transfer 149.25 µL of the culture medium into a centrifugation tube (1.5 mL).
Add 0.75 µL of 0.1 g/L of 3NT solution (internal standard).
Close the tubes and vortex well.
Add 150 µL of chilled at -20 °C methanol containing 1% (v/v) FA for sample deproteinization.
Close the tubes and vortex well.
Continue with sample preparation as described in section 3 (steps 3.3-3.11).
For samples secreting large amounts of Kyn, perform a 100-fold dilution with 0.1% (v/v) FA in water before analysis.
Prepare reference samples of standards for the calibration curve in 100 times diluted complete culture medium.
Alternatively, add more points in the calibration curve to adjust it to the concentration level of Kyn in the experimental sample if proper solubility and linearity are achieved.
Analyze the samples by LC-MS as described in section 5.
Construct a worklist and run each sample in triplicate.
Measure the peak area of analyte after completing the worklist.
Generate a spreadsheet using available software and obtain numerical data.
Calculate the ratio of the analyte peak area over the 3NT peak area in one spreadsheet column.
Use an individual linear calibration equation for each analyte to calculate concentrations of analytes in experimental samples.
Resuspend the cellular pellet with 100 μL of phosphate-buffered saline (PBS) in a 1.5 mL tube.

Prepare PBS by dissolving specified amounts of sodium chloride, potassium chloride, sodium phosphate dibasic, and potassium dihydrogen phosphate in ultrapure water, adjusting pH to 7.4 with hydrochloric acid.
Adjust the volume of PBS solution to 1 L with ultrapure water until homogeneous.
Freeze the samples at -20 °C and then defrost on ice; repeat this step 3 times.
Centrifuge the samples at 14,000 x g for 15 min at 4 °C.
Collect the supernatants into new tubes without disturbing the pellet.
Dilute the supernatants 10x with PBS.
Construct a calibration curve from 0 to 2 µg of protein per well range.
Prepare bovine serum albumin (BSA) standard solution by dissolving 1.23 μg of BSA in 1 mL ultrapure water and vortexing well.
Load different amounts of BSA standard solution on a 96-well plate: 0 µL, 2 µL, 4 µL, 5 µL, 7 µL, 10 µL, 15 µL, 20 µL.
Fill each well with PBS to a final volume of 50 µL.
Load 10 - 15 µL cell lysate into the wells on the same 96-well plate.
Add 200 µL of diluted Bradford reagent (diluted 5-times with ultrapure water) to each well.
Incubate the 96-well plate for at least 5 min at room temperature.
Measure absorbance at λ = 595 nm using a microplate reader.
Construct a calibration curve using a spreadsheet program by plotting BSA amount (µg) versus absorbance.
Add a linear trendline to the calibration curve and display the equation and regression coefficient on the chart.
Use the linear equation (y = ax +b, where y is absorbance at λ = 595 nm, a is slope, x is protein content (µg), b is curve intercept) to calculate protein amount in the sample.
Normalize kynurenine amount per 1 mg of total protein using the estimated protein content.
